title: Dedicated Capacity Stability Simulator and Customer Acceptance Protocol
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Purpose: Build a reproducible stability simulator and an associated customer acceptance protocol for Dedicated capacity that validates throughput guarantees, autoscaling behavior, and fleet control policies under realistic, time-varying workloads. This ticket scopes the simulator design, benchmarking methodology, canonical test scenarios, output telemetry requirements, and a runnable acceptance checklist we can hand to Sales/Onboarding and use during deployment signoffs.

Background: We have multiple Load/Replay and Prober artifacts scattered across engineering. Customers ask for deterministic acceptance runs that represent their mixed-priority traffic (chat + embeddings + reranking) and the autoscaling/fallback behaviors that matter for SLA. Existing suites focus on peak throughput but do not sufficiently exercise scale events, cache warm/cold cycles, or policy-driven routing changes.

Goals:
- Provide a simulator that can orchestrate multi-workload experiments (traffic mixes, token length distributions, priority skews, KV cache priming) against a Dedicated pool.
- Define a repeatable benchmarking methodology to report throughput, token/sec per-GPU, and tail latency (p50/p95/p99) across steady-state and transient scale events.
- Specify customer acceptance tests (CATs) with clear pass/fail criteria and required telemetry dashboards.
- Demonstrate autoscaling policy impact: test target-based scaling, queue-depth scaling, and scheduled scale events, and document safe rollback signals.

Out of scope: building an entirely new traffic generator language (we will extend existing runner); long-term CI integration (future ticket).

Deliverables:
1) Stability simulator runner extension with scenario DSL and YAML templates.
2) Benchmarking methodology doc (CSV + JSON artifacts format).
3) Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) checklist + scripts for running the CAT.
4) Observability dashboard template and alert rules for acceptance runs.

Key acceptance metrics (to be captured by the simulator):
- Sustained throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec) for each workload class.
- p50/p95/p99 generation latency for end-user visible requests.
- Tail latency under scale-up and scale-down events.
- Cold-start penalty (latency delta from warmed state).
- Queue depth and request rejection/drop rates.
- Autoscaling event timings (decision -> provisioning -> ready).
- Cost signal (estimated GPU-hours consumed during run).
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can run a templated 30-minute mixed workload (chat 60%, embedding 30%, rerank 10%) against a Dedicated pool and produce a single JSON summary with all key metrics.
Run artifacts are stored in /benchmarks/dedicated/stability/YYYYMMDD and contain traceable Git sha and config yaml.
CAT checklist contains 6 canonical scenarios and pass/fail thresholds; SRE and Solutions Eng approve the thresholds.
Dashboard and alert rules (p99 breach, queue growth, scaling failures) are deployed to staging and validate against the simulator runs.
A run demonstrating a policy-induced fallback (e.g., model variant fallback due to capacity limits) is reproducible and logged with routing decisions.
implementation_steps: Design scenario DSL: YAML schema to express workload mix, priority classes, token length distribution, KV cache priming steps, and node actions (drain, kill).
Add simulator hooks to orchestrate autoscaling experiments: trigger scale by policy, simulate delayed provisioning, and measure stabilization time.
Integrate with existing runner to emit OTEL traces and Prometheus-compatible metrics; produce final summary JSON and CSV artifacts.
Create 6 canonical scenarios: steady-state peak, ramp-up, ramp-down, intermittent bursts, cold-start recovery, and degraded-fallback path.
Implement CAT scripts that run the scenario collection, upload artifacts to the benchmark bucket, and snapshot dashboards.
Run cross-team validation with SRE, Solutions, and PM; iterate thresholds and annotated example reports for customers.
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL parsing and config validation (CI).
Small smoke run against a single-node Dedicated dev pool to validate basic metrics emission.
Full 30-minute staging runs across three Dedicated pool sizes (small/medium/large) to verify scaling and cost profiles.
Chaos tests: node drain during steady-state; verify request routing and fallback policy logs.
Customer acceptance rehearsal: run CAT with Solutions Eng using a synthetic customer config and collect signoff artifacts.
observability_and_outputs: Production-grade dashboard template with panels for per-route latency percentiles, token/sec, queue depth, and autoscaler state transitions.
Alert rules: p99 > SLA threshold for >2 minutes; queue depth growth > 2x baseline; failed scale events >1 in 10 mins.
Run artifact format: single JSON containing run metadata, per-workload time-series aggregates, and a CSV of sample latencies.
Linkable run report URL pattern for customer handoff and PSO playbooks.
customer_acceptance_tests: CAT-1 (SLA Smoke): 10-minute steady-state at requested commit capacity. Pass: >= 98% requests under SLA latency; no queue overflow.
CAT-2 (Scale Ramp): Gradual ramp to 3x baseline over 10 minutes. Pass: autoscaler adds nodes within configured SLA window and p95 remains within target.
CAT-3 (Burst Recovery): 30s high-intensity burst 5x baseline. Pass: system absorbs burst with <1% dropped requests and tail latency gracefully degrades but recovers within 3 minutes.
CAT-4 (Cold-Start): Run after full cache flush. Pass: cold penalty < defined threshold and warmup phase documented.
CAT-5 (Failover / Fallback): Simulate model variant unavailability causing route fallback. Pass: requests are rerouted, logs show policy decision, and customer-visible errors <=0.1%.
CAT-6 (Autoscaler Oscillation Guard): Introduce fluctuating traffic to validate scale cooldowns; Pass: no oscillation (node churn) > 1/minute.
rollout_and_communication: Phase 1: Internal staging runs and SRE signoff. Share example reports in #dedicated-capacity and attach to ticket.
Phase 2: Solutions Eng rehearsal with a pilot customer; update onboarding playbook with CAT steps and expected durations.
Phase 3: Gradual enablement to Sales/Onboarding team with a pre-baked benchmark template per customer tier.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Simulator may not faithfully reproduce certain customer traffic shapes (websocket streaming patterns). Mitigation: log gaps and add streaming scenario extension in follow-up ticket.
Risk: False positives from synthetic traffic (overly smooth arrivals). Mitigation: incorporate measured jitter profiles from production traces.
Risk: Observability cost of long runs. Mitigation: configurable sampling and summary export to reduce retention costs.
